 By Dilpreet Follow Add as Preferred Source Dilpreet has been covering football since 2020 and writing for Khel Now since 2025, covering World Football with a sharp perspective and a genuine passion for the game. Published at : November 14, 2026 at 4:26 PM (GMT+5:30) Modified at : November 14, 2026 at 4:26 PM (GMT+5:30) Neither of the last eight fixtures between these nations ended in a draw!
 The Japan national football team will lock horns with the Brazil national football team in what is going to be an international friendly contest. This high-voltage clash is all set to take place at the Singapore National Stadium.
 Japan are undefeated in their last four friendly outings and will be looking to add another win to their tally. They topped New Zealand 2-1 in their previous contest. The Samurai Blue will be confident for their next clash, but it won’t be an easy one.
 Hajime Moriyasu’s men are more than capable of establishing control in the game. They must not make a mistake by giving away the ball to their opponents.
 The Brazil national football team have also maintained an unbeaten run after their underwhelming World Cup campaign. They met Australia for two friendlies. In the first one, the five-time world champions were held to a 1-1 draw.
 They then made a strong comeback to bag a 4-2 victory in their second one. The team then also went on to secure a dominant 4-0 win against India.
 The Carlo Ancelotti-led side are all set to be in action once again. They are travelling away from the fixture, and this might make things a bit complicated for them. The strong squad quality is going to be their greatest weapon against the Samurai Blue.
 Players to Watch
 Catch Every Update, Anytime, Anywhere
 Ritsu Doan (Japan)
 The Eintracht Frankfurt man can help the Japan national football team both in the midfield and the attacking front. He can establish strong control of the midfield and is capable of running down the right flank with his fast pace. Ritsu Doan was one of the goal scorers for the Samurai Blue against New Zealand.
 He will be looking to engrave his name on the scoresheet once again.
 Raphinha (Brazil)
 Raphinha has been in a sensational run of form for FC Barcelona and will now look to display a similar show for the Brazil national football team. He can be deployed on the left wing as well as as a striker. With his current run of form, the 29-year-old is going to be a constant threat for the rivals.
